proposals.before: In the second year of Chengsheng (552), for repeated battle honors he was raised to marquis, his fief brought to five hundred households in all.
proposals.after: In the second year of Chengsheng (553), for repeated battle honors he was raised to marquis, his fief brought to five hundred households in all.
proposals.reason: Chengsheng began in AD 552; its second year corresponds to AD 553, not 552.

proposals.before: After Sihui was suppressed, in the second year of Shaotai (555) he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, stern-prestige general, and left defender of the heir.
proposals.after: After Sihui was suppressed, in the second year of Shaotai (556) he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, stern-prestige general, and left defender of the heir.
proposals.reason: Shaotai year one is AD 555; year two is AD 556.

proposals.before: In the fifth year of Tiancheng (564), Emperor Wen again decreed: "Han worthies were painted in the palace; Wei champions were named in the ancestral shrine—so merit lives on and ages do not forget.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of Tianjia (564), Emperor Wen again decreed: "Han worthies were painted in the palace; Wei champions were named in the ancestral shrine—so merit lives on and ages do not forget.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: In the fifth year of Tiancheng, Emperor Wen again issued an edict saying: "Han dynasty meritorious ministers had their forms painted in the palace halls; Wei dynasty fierce generals had their names joined to the ancestral temple—thus merit endures and generations do not forget.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of Tianjia, Emperor Wen again issued an edict saying: "Han dynasty meritorious ministers had their forms painted in the palace halls; Wei dynasty fierce generals had their names joined to the ancestral temple—thus merit endures and generations do not forget.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.after: Cheng Lingxi, styled Xuandi, was a native of Haining in Xin'an.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Tiancheng (563) Zhou Di raided Linchuan again. Lingxi was made commander and, marching from Poyang by a separate route, drove Di back into the hills.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Tianjia (563) Zhou Di raided Linchuan again. Lingxi was made commander and, marching from Poyang by a separate route, drove Di back into the hills.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Tiancheng, Zhou Di again raided Linchuan heavily; Lingxi was made commander-in-chief; from a separate route through Poyang he struck Di, and Di again fled into the mountain valleys.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Tianjia, Zhou Di again raided Linchuan heavily; Lingxi was made commander-in-chief; from a separate route through Poyang he struck Di, and Di again fled into the mountain valleys.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made pacifying-west general and grand master with the golden seal and purple cord, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made garrisoning-west general and opener of an office equal to the three dukes, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
proposals.reason: 鎮西將軍 is not the same as 安西/pacifying-west; 開府儀同三司 is not 'grand master with the golden seal and purple cord'.

decisions.reason: 承聖二年 is Chengsheng year 2. Chengsheng began in AD 552, so year 2 is AD 553; the parenthetical 552 is wrong.
紹泰二年 is Shaotai year 2. Shaotai year 1 is AD 555, so year 2 is AD 556; the parenthetical 555 is wrong.
天嘉五年 uses 嘉, the Chen reign Tianjia; Tiancheng misreads the era name. The replacement restores Tianjia while keeping the correct AD 564.
Same unit: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng. The literal replacement matches the Chinese reign name.
字玄滌 is a two-character courtesy name Xuandi (玄+滌); Xuantidi invents a third syllable absent from the Chinese.
Same unit: 玄滌 is Xuandi. The literal replacement removes the invented syllable.
天嘉四年 is Tianjia year 4; Tiancheng misreads 嘉. Tianjia restores the correct reign name.
Same unit: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng. The literal replacement matches the Chinese reign name.
贈鎮西將軍、開府儀同三司 names Garrisoning-West General and opener of an office equal to the three dukes; pacifying-west and golden-seal-and-purple-cord are different titles (安西 / 金紫光祿大夫).
